title: Map of New South Wales showing location of the main types of rural production
description: [Sydney] : [publisher not identified], [1966?] 1 map : colour ; 42 x 50 cm
notes: Map of New South Wales showing major agricultural regions producing wheat, beef, Merino wool and dairy products, boundaries of milk zone as at January, 1966, limits to major beef cattle areas and western limits of beef production, major districts producing special products such as rice, poultry, eggs, potatoes, vegetables, sugar cane, cotton, citrus, lucerne hay, grapes, bananas, pome and stone fruits.

title: Map of New South Wales showing pastoral stations &c. / by H.E.C. Robinson
description: Sydney : H.E.C. Robinson, [1905?] 1 map : colour, mounted on linen ; 100 x 135 cm, on sheet 105 x 144 cm
notes: Cadastral map of New South Wales showing railways constructed, pastoral holdings, homesteads, state and territorial boundaries, the Eastern, Central and Western Divisions are defined by colour, Pastures Protection Districts (Under Act of 1902) are delineated (orange). Relief shown by hachures. "N.B. - The publisher is indebted to Mr. Alex Wilson for much of the pastoral information shown on this map." Includes index to pastoral stations.

title: Plan of the town of Sydney New South Wales shewing Common [cartographic material]
notes: "59637". Map is facsimile. Map of Sydney shewing buildings, streets, old toll houses and the boundaries of Sydney Common "as described in General Order of 5th October 1811". MAP F 868 copy Also available online https://nla.gov.au/nla.obj-230009455 Ferguson Collection Map F 868.

title: Liverpool, New South Wales / produced by Royal Australian Survey Corps, 1955
description: [Canberra] : Royal Australian Survey Corps, 1955 1 map : colour ; 48 x 77 cm, on sheet 61 x 85 cm.
notes: Topographic map of Liverpool region, New South Wales, showing roads, bridges, railway, telegraph or telephone and electric transmission lines, buildings, aerodromes, water features, and vegetation. Relief shown by contours and spot heights. Map annotated with: "Boundary of Holsworthy manoeuvre area and location of sentry posts". "Air photography: 87 (PR) Squadron, Royal Australian Air Force, Mission Number I56/5/422 Liverpool Area, 1949". "Compilation: Compiled by the Royal Australian Survey Corps from ground surveys and air photographs 1952". "AHQ/A2-6/0247". "AHQ/MISC/1188A". Includes index to adjoining sheets, magnetic declination and reliability diagrams, legend, and grid referencing guide. National Library of Australia's designation of sheet number: I 56 5 422. Also available online http://nla.gov.au/nla.obj-446273750

description: Sydney : N.S.W. Dept. of Mines, 1968 1 map : col. ; 48 x 61 cm., on sheet 65 x 82 cm. + booklet (33 p).
notes: Geological map of the Angledool region showing geological boundaries, bores, sub-surface contours, roads, mineral deposits and geological information. Relief shown by contours and spot heights. Accompanied by booklet: 1:250,000 geological series explanatory notes Angledool / A.C. Offenberg. [Sydney] : Dept. of Mines, Geological Survey of New South Wales, 1967. "Topographic base compiled by Royal Australian Survey Corps in 1962 from 1959 aerial photography". "Compiled by: A. C. Offenberg (1966)". Includes index to adjoining sheets, geological reliability diagram and cross section.

title: Brindabella, New South Wales [cartographic material] / [prepared by the National Capital Development Commission]
description: [196-?] 1 map : b&w, mounted on linen ; 45 x 74 cm. on sheet 48 x 77 cm.
notes: Caption title. Unpublished photoreproduction of a composite map from what appears to be a series of overlapping aerial photographs of the mountainous region comprising the Murrumbidgee River region in western Australian Capital Territory on the right extending to its western boundary and further west to the Goobarragandra River and the Micalong Swamp. The Brindabella Ranges run somewhere in the middle of the map. A white grid has been imposed across these conjoined images with approximate latitude and longitudes. "8-450".
